title: Giants on the Frontier - Nightstone Chapter 1 expanded
tagline: A richer Chapter 1 play guide for Nightstone, the ruined village, the rescue path, the Dripping Caves, and the strange giant tower.
sourceNote: Not official WotC content. This is an original scaffold inspired by the Nightstone chapter; use your owned book/PDF for exact narration, maps, treasure, and stat blocks.
campaignGuide: Use this expanded Chapter 1 template to run Nightstone as a connected investigation and rescue. Open the village slowly, avoid inventing an organized guard force, and let the ringing bell be a clue, not a welcome signal. Nightstone is abandoned by villagers but not empty: two worgs are feeding in the square, two goblins are ringing the chapel bell, and scattered goblin looters occupy towers, farms, the inn pantry, the trading post, and the windmill. Map-aware routing matters: the building left of the drawbridge approach is area 5, the temple with the bell; the graveyards and Nandar crypt are area 6, including a possible quiet route behind the temple; the inn is area 8 east of that route. KEEP AND BRIDGE (important continuity): Nandar Keep stands on a raised motte to the south, joined to the village bailey only by a long, sloped stone bridge. A giant's falling rock destroyed the bridge's middle span, so the keep is CUT OFF from the village and cannot simply be walked to. Never describe the keep bridge as intact, lowered, or freely crossable, and do not present a separate 'keep drawbridge' the party can stroll over. Reaching the keep means crossing the broken gap: only a strong character (Strength 15+) can attempt the running jump, and the landing is a check (about DC 10 Athletics jumping up-slope, or DC 10 Acrobatics down-slope) with a short fall and a little bludgeoning damage on a failure. Do not confuse this broken keep bridge with the village's own palisade drawbridge, which the fleeing villagers left lowered as the way into the village. KEEP IS DAMAGED BUT NOT EMPTY (important continuity): cut off does NOT mean deserted. If the party crosses the gap into Nandar Keep, they find survivors, not silence. The great hall (area 14A) holds a handful of demoralized, shell-shocked keep guards (for example Sydiri Haunlar, Torem Breck, Alara Winterspell, and Kaelen Zam) gathered around the body of Lady Velrosa Nandar, the High Steward, who was killed when the giants' bombardment collapsed the keep. The guards have no clear leader, are arguing about what to do next, and will look to capable newcomers for guidance; they can describe the giant attack, the broken bridge, and that the villagers fled north. The inner bailey and damaged gatehouses also hold the bodies of guards killed by falling rocks. NEVER portray the keep as empty or call out to find no one there: acknowledge these surviving guards when the party reaches the keep. NIGHTSTONE INN AND KELLA (area 8 — important continuity, the inn is NOT empty): the inn is owned by the shield dwarf Morak Ur'gray, who led the villagers to the Dripping Caves. In the dining room (8A), a giant's rock punched through the roof; lying in the open in the middle of the floor is a DEAD GOBLIN with a fresh crossbow bolt in its chest — this corpse is obvious on sight, always describe it. A Wisdom (Medicine) check (about DC 10) shows the goblin died only minutes ago, implying a hidden, recent shooter. Characters in the dining room can also HEAR someone rummaging in the kitchen. In the kitchen/pantry (8B) a goblin named Gum-Gum is noisily looting food into a heavy sack; she is easy to find by sound and flees if confronted. Hiding in the shadows of the wrecked room above the dining room (8F) is KELLA DARKHOPE, a Zhentarim spy disguised as a traveling monk; she shot the goblin and watches the dining room through the hole in her floor. She stays hidden until her Zhentarim allies (the 'Seven Snakes') arrive; spotting her requires a Wisdom (Perception) check contested by her Stealth. If discovered she pretends to be an ordinary guest knocked unconscious by falling debris and left behind, lying that the goblins have nothing to do with the giants — see through the ruse with a Wisdom (Insight) check contested by her Charisma (Deception). A Zhentarim flying snake coils around her arm, carrying a parchment that reads 'On our way.' NEVER portray the inn as deserted: the dead goblin is in plain view, Gum-Gum is audible in the kitchen, and Kella is hidden above; a player who searches or fails to spot Kella should still be given grounded hints (the fresh kill, the sense of being watched), not an empty room. SPECIAL EVENTS (use these EXACT names and facts — never invent substitute names). SEVEN SNAKES: after the goblins are cleared (before the party can finish a long rest), seven Zhentarim mercenaries ride in on horseback and call out for Kella Darkhope. Their leader is XOLKIN ALASSANDAR, a lawful-evil male HALF-ELF bandit captain — charming, ruthless, mid-thirties; he commands six human bandit subordinates, and together they are known as the Seven Snakes, doing dirty work for a Zhent leader called the Snail based in Daggerford. Their goal is to turn Nightstone into a base for the Zhentarim (the Black Network). Xolkin is in love with Kella: if she is a prisoner he offers gemstones (five 100 gp gems) for her freedom or frees her by force; in a fight he drinks a potion of invulnerability. He wears a gold ring bearing the Zhentarim symbol, a black winged serpent. The Seven Snakes ignore the cut-off keep. The leader is ALWAYS Xolkin Alassandar — never rename him. EAR SEEKERS: after the Seven Snakes event, orcs of the Ear Seekers tribe (they wear necklaces of elf ears) flee south after losing a battle to the wood elves of the Ardeep Forest and try to storm Nightstone. Their war chief is GURRASH, already wounded by elven arrows (about 60 hit points left), leading roughly twenty orcs plus his Eye of Gruumsh lieutenant NORGRA ONE-EYE, who takes command if Gurrash dies. The orcs fight to the death, take no prisoners, and ignore the keep. If the party is being overwhelmed, eight wood elf scouts of the Ardeep Forest led by ROND ARROWHOME arrive from the north, help defeat the orcs, then leave with a shouted 'You're welcome!' wanting no reward. Use these exact names (Gurrash, Norgra One-Eye, Rond Arrowhome) — never invent substitutes. The villagers fled toward the hills and were captured by goblins in the caves. The tower of Zephyros appears after the rescue and moves the story from village aftermath into the giant conflict. Keep the book outside version control and use it for exact room keys, names, and future giant politics.

road-to-nightstone.goal: Approach Nightstone and understand that the village has been abandoned after a recent attack.
road-to-nightstone.starter: The road climbs into wind-scoured hills. Ahead, Nightstone sits quiet behind a broken palisade, its drawbridge lowered and its square empty.
choices: Look for signs of recent battle
road-to-nightstone.guidance: Set the tone with a silent, damaged frontier village. Emphasize the low hum of activity, shredded sails, and a distant bell. Avoid making the party feel welcomed. If the players ask where people are, answer that the streets are empty and the village looks abandoned. Use a moderate Investigation or Perception check to reveal fresh tracks leading inward. Advance to the next scene once they commit to entering Nightstone.

open-palisade.goal: Enter Nightstone and confirm that the palisade and gate mean the village was overwhelmed, not defended.
open-palisade.starter: The palisade gate is open. Streaks of fresh mud and blood darken the timbers, but no watch is posted and no answering shout comes from inside.
choices: Scan the tops of the walls
open-palisade.guidance: This scene is about the first impression of Nightstone. The defenders did not greet the party; the place feels abandoned and unsafe. If the party searches, let them find evidence of people fleeing, something large striking the village, and goblin-sized tracks near the gate and towers. There is one goblin looter in the east tower and two in the southeast tower if the party searches those towers closely. The drawbridge here is the VILLAGE palisade drawbridge, left lowered by fleeing villagers. If the party heads south toward Nandar Keep or asks about the keep's bridge or gate, remember the keep is cut off: the bridge to the motte has a destroyed middle span and cannot be walked across intact. Describe the broken gap and the keep as unreachable without a running jump, never as an intact keep drawbridge. Guide them toward the village square or the chapel bell rather than into random buildings.

village-square.goal: Discover the missing megalith, damaged homes, and a pattern of forced evacuation.
village-square.starter: The village square is littered with smashed stone and overturned carts. Two worgs snarl over a dead dog near the open center, where a wide patch of bare earth marks where the central megalith once stood.
village-square.guidance: Use this scene to show that Nightstone was attacked from above and that the villagers fled, but do not present it as an empty safe square. Two worgs are present in the square and attack intruders. If the player wants to avoid the worgs instead of fighting, support map-aware tactics: sneak along the left side toward the temple, use rubble and walls as cover, slip behind the temple into the graveyard/crypt area, or continue east toward the inn. Resolve this with Stealth, Perception, or tactical movement instead of forcing an attack. After the worg threat is handled, investigation can reveal that the stone is gone, the damage came from a powerful aerial bombardment, and the villagers fled rather than defended the settlement. If the party tries to reach Nandar Keep on the motte to the south, the bridge connecting it to the village is broken (its middle span destroyed by a falling rock), leaving the keep cut off; describe the broken gap rather than an intact crossing. If combat gets loud after the bell has been stopped, nearby goblin looters may investigate from adjacent locations. Keep official location names vague and refer the player to their book for exact maps and treasures.

chapel-bell.goal: Track the ringing bell and understand that it is part of the mystery rather than a normal alarm.
chapel-bell.starter: A slow, lonely bell rings from the village chapel. It sounds more like a signal from a frightened survivor than a welcome alarm.
chapel-bell.guidance: The bell should feel eerie. This is area 5, the village temple dedicated to dawn and forest deities. It has a main worship room with benches, stained glass, a pulpit, and a dirt floor; the back room/steeple area contains the bell rope and a looted acolyte bedroom. The cause is specific: two goblins named Beedo and Vark in the back room/steeple area are playing with the bell rope. If the party approaches carefully, let them notice that the ringing continues despite no obvious guard force. The temple's west-side/back access connects naturally to area 6, the graveyards, so sneaking behind the temple toward the Nandar crypt or toward the inn is a valid player route. Use Stealth or Perception to detect the goblins before they notice the party. Once the bell is silenced or its meaning is clear, move the story along.

goblin-scouts.goal: Confront the goblins looting the village and learn the direction the villagers were forced to go.
goblin-scouts.starter: Small goblins slip between ruined cottages with stolen goods, keeping to the shadows and avoiding the bell's sound.
goblin-scouts.guidance: Run the goblins as opportunistic looters using the abandoned village. They may fight, flee, or bargain. Concrete looter count for the DM: one goblin in the east tower, two in the southeast tower, two in the Southwell farm yard, two at the Nesper farm, one in the stable hayloft, one named Gum-Gum in the inn kitchen or pantry, one in the trading post, two in the windmill, and two named Beedo and Vark in the chapel/steeple bell scene. Area 8, the inn, also contains the Kella thread: Morak led villagers away, Kella stayed behind as a disguised guest/spy, a freshly killed goblin in the damaged dining room points to her, and she can watch from the broken upper room. At least one captured goblin should reveal that the villagers ran toward the hills and that goblins took captives into nearby caves. This scene should transition the party from village exploration into the rescue path.

trail-to-caves.goal: Follow tracks from Nightstone to the cave entrance and prepare for a rescue mission.
trail-to-caves.starter: The trail leads away from the burned-out cottages into the foothills, with a mix of boot prints, dragged packs, and smaller goblin footprints heading toward a damp cave mouth.
trail-to-caves.guidance: This connective scene helps the party shift from the village to the caves. Allow Survival or Investigation checks to reveal signs of a forced march, a struggle, and a guarded entrance. Keep the actual cave layout for the book. Use this scene to build tension and set up the rescue; then advance when the party is ready to enter the Dripping Caves.

dripping-caves.goal: Rescue the captured villagers from goblins and their stronger allies in the caves.
dripping-caves.starter: The cave smells of damp stone, smoke, and uneasy captives. Echoes of snarling voices and chained prisoners come from deeper chambers.
dripping-caves.guidance: This is the rescue encounter. The caverns are controlled by goblins and may include one stronger brute. Allow for stealth, social rescue, or combat solutions. The exact cave rooms and prisoner locations belong to the book; use this scene to capture the general encounter and to empower the party to free some captives. Record who was rescued and what the party learns from them.

tower-of-zephyros.goal: Encounter the giant tower and use it as the bridge to the next giant-focused chapter.
tower-of-zephyros.starter: After the caves, a massive tower appears on the horizon, gliding over the hills like a slow storm cloud.
tower-of-zephyros.guidance: This scene should launch the next act of the campaign. The giant tower is a dramatic transition. Use your owned book for the giant's exact personality, the tower's interior, and the destination. The key point is to link the rescue at Nightstone with the larger giant crisis and motivate the party to continue.

endingMessage: The party has reached the end of Chapter 1: Nightstone is quiet again, the villagers are rescued, and the tower of Zephyros now promises a new direction. Record the giant facts, any rescued villagers, and the next destination.

npcs.name: Nightstone survivor
npcs.description: A frightened villager rescued from the caves or found near the village.
knowledge: The village was struck by a giant force and then looted by goblins.
The villagers fled toward the hills and were taken into the Dripping Caves.

npcs.name: Captured goblin
npcs.description: A nervous goblin scout who can reveal where the villagers were taken.
knowledge: We took prisoners from Nightstone into the caves.
Goblins are holding captives in the dripping caverns under the hill.

npcs.name: Tower messenger
npcs.description: A giant envoy or otherworldly herald connected to the tower of Zephyros.
knowledge: The tower is a moving stronghold tied to the giant crisis.
The party's next goal is beyond Nightstone, toward the giant's circle.

mock.socialSuccess: The survivor shares useful details about the attack, the caves, and the tower, making the next objective clear.
mock.socialFailure: The survivor is too shaken to answer clearly and needs more reassurance before they explain anything important.
mock.explorationSuccess: Your investigation confirms the village was evacuated under duress, traces lead toward the hills, and the next step is to follow the cave trail.
mock.explorationFailure: You sense something is wrong and the village is not safe, but the full story is still hidden. Try another detail or move to the next clue.
mock.canonFactOnSocialSuccess: Villagers from Nightstone were captured and taken into the Dripping Caves.
